extracted.intended_audience: Washington Post reporters, editors, and newsroom staff (newsroom journalists)
extracted.subtask_description: House rules and evaluative criteria for reporting, editing, and publishing news at The Washington Post, covering ethics, accuracy, fairness, sourcing, and newsworthiness. Intended to guide newsroom decisions and conduct (including social media) to serve readers and the truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Mission
rubrics_metrics.description: "The highest duty is to its readers and to the truth."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committed to transparency, innovation and accuracy in delivering authoritative reporting and commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: No gifts from news sources; No free trips; No preferential treatment sought or accepted; No active involvement in partisan causes (politics, community, demonstrations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards are stricter than typical private business norms — avoid arrangements or behavior that could create even the appearance of bias or preferential treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness (completeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: "No story is fair if it omits facts of major importance or significance. Fairness includes completeness."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reporting includes all facts of major importance; avoid leaving out context or facts that would materially change readers' understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose information sources to maximum extent
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose information sources to maximum extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about how information was obtained unless there is a compelling, documented reason to protect a source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Right of reply for subjects of negative coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer subjects the opportunity to respond to negative allegations or reporting; include their responses in coverage when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple sources for damaging claims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corroborate allegations that could harm reputations with independent confirmation from multiple sources before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify before publishing; Correct errors promptly; Avoid speculation framed as fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm facts and documents, attribute appropriately, publish corrections quickly and visibly when mistakes occur; do not present unverified conjecture as established fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymous Sources — Sparingly used; Editor approval required; Reasoning explained to readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use anonymity only when necessary (e.g., safety or severe risk), secure editorial sign-off, and explain to readers why anonymity was granted and what corroboration exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards Desk oversight and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards Desk (2022) — Dedicated team to update, explain and enforce policies; create new standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Standards Desk as a resource for policy interpretation, rule updates, and enforcement; consult them for unclear or novel situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance of facts (omitting important facts = unfair).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize facts of public importance; assess whether information materially affects readers' understanding or public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient background and context so readers can evaluate the meaning and implications of reported facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source diversity / multi-sourcing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek multiple, independent sources and a range of perspectives to avoid one-sided reporting and to corroborate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public significance over commercial appeal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate stories primarily by their public-interest value rather than by potential for clicks, advertising, or commercial benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth over haste
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor verification and accuracy even when pressured by speed; avoid rushing to publish unverified information for timeliness alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from sources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain editorial independence — do not let sources dictate coverage, and avoid relationships that could compromise impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for clear, confident reporting grounded in verified facts and responsible attribution; avoid tentative language that confuses facts with opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation in form
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue new storytelling formats and tools while preserving core standards of accuracy, fairness, and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about methods
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain reporting methods, sourcing decisions, and limitations to readers where relevant to build trust and allow independent assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Same values apply: professionalism, empathy, focus on facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply newsroom standards to staff behavior on social platforms — be professional, empathetic, factual, and avoid partisan or activist engagement that conflicts with newsroom independence.
